items.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007
items.q: Bobo Rudd I particularly remember, he was a great English teacher. I took every course that he taught.

ctx.x: When you were a junior and senior in high school, were you worried or concerned about World War II and what that was going to mean for you?

Yea. I was too young for service. And there were fifty some students here when I came, when I entered in the summer program. And I didn’t know when they’d draft me but I went anyway and — the guidance counselor here was very good. He was excellent. He said, “Don’t worry about it.” He said, “You just go away until they send you that jolly little message in the mail and you’ll be fine.” But the school itself was wonderful. They practically had a teacher for every three or four students. It was just great. It was a…
While you were here there probably was a significant number of veterans coming back from the war. Did they talk much about their experiences?
